newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open lower after stock rise.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open lower after stock rise.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were seen opening slightly lower Friday, in line with LME copper after a further rise in LME warehouse copper stocks.
But activity was again expected to be limited, with a bank holiday in London Monday slowing trade.
COMEX July copper was seen opening down 0.25 to 0.75 cent a pound from Thursday's close at 109.85 cents, after trading a 110.10-108.85 range in overnight ACCESS trade.
LME copper stocks rose a further 2,175 tonnes Friday to 147,925 tonnes, while COMEX stocks slipped fell another 637 short tons Thursday to 48,883 short tons.
Trading was likely to be light in world copper markets again Friday though, after May Day holidays in much of continental Europe Thursday and ahead of the U.K. bank holiday Monday, traders said.
But despite the slippage in copper prices this week, the market was still seen underpinned by solid U.S. economic growth, with a supply surplus now seen less likely this year, analysts said.
